faqs.a: Density = mass / volume. A 500 g block occupying 250 cm3 has density 500 / 250 = 2 g/cm3.
Rearrange the formula: mass = density x volume. Aluminum (2.7 g/cm3) filling 100 cm3 weighs 2.7 x 100 = 270 g.
faqs.q: How do I find mass from density?

faqs.a: Volume = mass / density. 500 g of water (1 g/cm3) occupies 500 / 1 = 500 cm3, which is 500 mL.
faqs.q: How do I find volume from density?

faqs.a: 1 g/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3. Multiply g/cm3 by 1000 to get kg/m3.
faqs.q: How do I convert g/cm3 to kg/m3?

faqs.a: Yes: 1 mL = 1 cm3 exactly, so they are interchangeable in these calculations.
faqs.q: Is 1 mL the same as 1 cm3?

keyFacts: Density is mass per unit volume: p = m / V.
Water's density is 1 g/cm3 (1000 kg/m3) at 4 C — the reference for specific gravity.
Objects denser than their fluid sink; less dense ones float.
Density of gases is usually given in kg/m3 or g/L.
Temperature changes density slightly, especially for gases.

density-calculator.workedExample:
A metal block weighs 500 g and displaces 250 cm3 of water:

1. Density = mass / volume = 500 / 250 = 2 g/cm3.
2. In kg/m3: 2 x 1000 = 2000 kg/m3 — close to aluminum (2700 kg/m3), so it is a lighter alloy.
3. Solving for mass instead: a 100 cm3 piece of the same metal weighs 2 x 100 = 200 g.

The same three numbers rearrange to answer any of the three questions.
